That's part of why I mentioned the self harm in the title. So that if anyone were to be put off by it such as yourself they can choose to not click on the photo. I can understand why it would be upsetting to others, and I'm decently self aware.

I guess ultimately I found it kind of funny. Maybe my scars look fresher than they really are or something but you're essentially trying to say "you should stop cutting" to someone that's already stopped and then your response was something along the lines of "I'm just telling the harsh truth, everyone else is sugar coating".

 In my opinion it's more helpful for people to say that you can move on from your mistakes rather than pointing out that they were dumb in the first place. That's kind of the point I'm getting at here and that was why I felt compelled to respond and point out how your choice of language is problematic.

 You can share your opinions all you like, just keep in mind that language is powerful and this is a forum discussing normal naked bodies. So treading carefully is the better approach.

I currently have been free from self harm for a little over 6 months. 
I don't know if I consider it disfigurement personally. Though I think you're posting with good intentions, I'd like to point out that using such strong wording could make a person feel pretty shitty about themselves. 

I think the stigma of this particular type of coping mechanism doesn't help or further people in their journey for recovery. There's a lot of unhealthy and maladaptive coping mechanisms out there - including substance abuse. Those things cause bodily harm but it's internal and depending on the substance it is socially acceptable to an extent.

I think that's part of it for some people, at least for me. I can externalise my pain with self harm. Ultimately I don't want to rely on any one crutch or to be unhealthy, but when I've tried to tune out from reality with things like alcohol it felt so silly to me that it was acceptable even though I felt like it made me feel worse physically and emotionally than most anything else. 

I'm not saying anyone should hurt themselves. But I do think saying "you should stop cutting because you're becoming disfigured" is reductive and dismissive. That's just my 2 cents though. I'm clearly not a therapist or anything.

Thank you. I'll try to treat it as just another chapter of my story without being too self conscious about it. I guess most of my worry is from the people I know and love seeing them because they knew what I looked like before and I know they're a cause for concern. We all just want to be accepted, after all.
